sources.title: Monetary policy assessment of 24 September 2026
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss CPI through Aug 2026; policy decision 24 Sep 2026; conditional forecast 2026–2028
sources.revision: September 2026 forecast vintage; conditional on policy rate 0% throughout forecast horizon
sources.units: Policy rate: % p.a.; CPI: % y/y and annual average
sources.scopeAndLimits: Documents CPI, exchange-rate context, FX intervention willingness, policy setting, inflation forecast and growth outlook. Does not establish causal CHF effects; forecast is conditional, not realized observation.

sources.title: Safe haven currencies and the euro
sources.observedPeriod: Historical exchange-rate and risk episodes covered by study (paper vintage 2013)
sources.revision: Working-paper vintage; historical sample; inspect paper for exact end date and specifications
sources.units: Exchange-rate returns / risk measures
sources.scopeAndLimits: Documents bilateral and time-varying safe-haven patterns; CHF does not uniformly appreciate against every currency in risk episodes. Historical correlation/decomposition does not identify a universal causal elasticity or future capital flow.

sources.title: The speed of exchange rate pass-through
sources.observedPeriod: Daily Swiss import transaction data around 15 Jan 2015 CHF appreciation
sources.revision: Working-paper vintage; 2015 event study
sources.units: Import unit values; pass-through elasticities
sources.evidenceRole: Scholarly empirical source with transaction-level data
sources.scopeAndLimits: Studies unusually sharp 2015 shock and invoice currency. Import-price evidence is not a current CPI forecast or export elasticity; external validity to different shocks is uncertain.

sources.title: Exchange rate pass-through in Switzerland: Evidence from vector autoregressions
sources.observedPeriod: Monthly price data 1976–2004
sources.revision: Historical sample ending 2004; model vintage 2007
sources.units: Import prices and consumer prices; impulse responses
sources.scopeAndLimits: Finds pass-through to import prices exceeds pass-through to aggregate CPI, and CPI pass-through weakened in low/stable inflation period. Old sample and recursive VAR identification limit current quantitative transfer.

sources.title: The exchange rate elasticity of the Swiss current account
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss current-account and exchange-rate historical sample (see paper tables)
sources.revision: Working-paper vintage 2022; revisions not stated on landing page
sources.units: Current account components; exchange-rate elasticities
sources.scopeAndLimits: Useful counterweight on aggregate current-account/exchange-rate responses. Current-account balances mix goods, services and incomes and do not map directly to GDP or firm profits.

sources.title: 2025: Exports hit a new record, driven by chemicals and pharmaceuticals
sources.publisher: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG)
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss customs goods trade, calendar year 2025
sources.revision: Annual 2025 release; customs statistics vintage released 29 Jan 2026
sources.units: Nominal goods exports/imports, CHF; growth rates
sources.scopeAndLimits: Aggregate merchandise trade excludes services and does not show company-level currency exposure, domestic value added, real quantities or hedging. Use linked detailed tables for sector breakdown and note customs conventions.

sources.title: Swiss balance of payments and international investment position: 2025 and Q4 2025
sources.observedPeriod: Balance of payments and IIP: 2025 and 2025-Q4
sources.revision: Annual/Q4 release vintage 24 Mar 2026; SNB data may be revised
sources.units: CHF billion; current and financial account flows; IIP stocks
sources.scopeAndLimits: Separates transaction flows and external positions; current-account balances do not equal domestic production or disposable income; non-monetary gold and merchanting can cause large gross flows.

sources.title: Swiss balance of payments and international investment position: Q2 2026
sources.observedPeriod: Balance of payments and IIP: 2026-Q2
sources.revision: Quarterly preliminary vintage released 22 Sep 2026; subject to revisions
sources.units: CHF billion; quarterly flows and positions
sources.evidenceRole: Primary official external accounts, latest identified quarterly vintage by cutoff
sources.scopeAndLimits: Q2 2026 results are flow/position statistics and not a causal commodity-trading shock measure. Release notes merchanting and non-monetary gold drove year-on-year goods balance movements.

sources.title: Notes to the current account survey (CAS): merchanting definitions and reporting
sources.observedPeriod: Current account survey definitions; living methodological page
sources.revision: Living methodology page accessed 2026-10-14; publication date not disclosed
sources.units: BPM6-aligned transactions; sales, purchases, services and merchanting
sources.scopeAndLimits: Defines merchanting as resident purchase and resale of goods abroad without goods entering Switzerland/Liechtenstein. Gross merchanting turnover is not domestic value added; distinguish merchanting margin, services and derivatives/margin payments.

sources.title: The Swiss commodities sector: current situation and outlook
sources.publisher: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), Interdepartmental Platform on Commodities
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss commodities sector; empirical inputs largely through 2016–2017 as documented in report
sources.revision: Federal Council assessment/report 2018; contains dated legacy estimates and wide measurement uncertainty
sources.units: Employment, trade-finance funding, tax, transit trade; units vary by chapter
sources.evidenceRole: Primary government assessment with commissioned studies
sources.scopeAndLimits: Explicitly says firms not separately classified and sector size/value-added estimates vary materially; legacy employment and funding estimates must not be treated as current. Supports mapping data limitations, not a precise contemporary GDP share.

sources.title: Merchanting and Current Account Balances
sources.observedPeriod: Cross-country panel 53 countries, 1980–2011
sources.revision: Working-paper vintage 2013; panel ends 2011
sources.units: Current-account balance (% GDP); panel estimates
sources.scopeAndLimits: Finds merchanting can increase measured current-account surplus while earnings are reinvested abroad rather than domestic investment. Cross-country average is not a Switzerland-specific current causal estimate.

sources.title: Dispatch on the Switzerland-EU Package (Bilaterals III)
sources.publisher: Federal Department of Foreign Affairs (FDFA), Directorate for European Affairs
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss–EU package status as of 13 Mar 2026; agreements signed 2 Mar 2026; parliamentary dispatch
sources.revision: Official dispatch and agreement texts; signature is not ratification or entry into force
sources.units: Legal status and agreement text; no economic units
sources.scopeAndLimits: Confirms 2 Mar 2026 signatures and 13 Mar dispatch to Parliament. Package remains subject to Swiss parliamentary/democratic approval and EU procedures; no general effective date established by the dispatch page. Do not model proposed provisions as already effective.

sources.title: Federal Council adopts the Swiss–EU relations package: parliamentary and referendum status updates
sources.observedPeriod: Package status and political/legal process through 12 Aug 2026
sources.revision: Living official page; includes dated entries; accessed at 2026-10-14 cutoff
sources.units: Legal process milestones
sources.scopeAndLimits: Documents parliamentary stage, Federal Council actions and referendum-related debate. Check each dated update and component; no blanket enactment/effective date may be inferred.

sources.title: Electricity agreement Switzerland–EU
sources.observedPeriod: Negotiated agreement signed 2 Mar 2026; parliamentary phase began after Mar 2026 dispatch
sources.revision: Living page; publication date not disclosed
sources.units: Legal status; electricity system integration and security-of-supply pathways
sources.evidenceRole: Primary official sector status and policy source
sources.scopeAndLimits: States Swiss grid is physically integrated but lacks legal guarantees under status quo, and describes agreement purpose. Signed agreement is still in parliamentary phase, so prospective benefits are not realized outcomes.

sources.title: Horizon package 2021–2027: Switzerland participation status
sources.publisher: State Secretariat for Education, Research and Innovation (SERI/SBFI)
sources.observedPeriod: EU programme participation from programme year 2025; status updated for 2026–2027 calls
sources.revision: Living status page; EUPA signed 10 Nov 2025; accessed 2026-10-14
sources.units: Programme eligibility, contributions and grants; EUR/CHF where in programme documents
sources.scopeAndLimits: EUPA allows retroactive association to Horizon Europe, Euratom and Digital Europe from 1 Jan 2025; differs from package-wide ratification. Program-specific eligibility, funding commitments and implementation timing must be checked separately; grants do not instantaneously raise productivity.

sources.title: Strengthening economic resilience within global value chains: OECD Economic Surveys—Switzerland 2024
sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss trade openness, supply-chain and FDI evidence; underlying observations vary, primarily pre-2024
sources.revision: Economic Survey 2024; underlying sources/years stated by chart and section
sources.units: Trade and FDI shares; value added; trade costs
sources.evidenceRole: Intergovernmental analytical report using official data and cited studies
sources.scopeAndLimits: Documents openness and diversification/resilience trade-offs, EU access, and chemicals/pharma export concentration. Aggregates and cited literature do not identify causal friendshoring gains; report predates 2026 legal package status.

sources.title: The impact of exchange rate fluctuations on markups: firm-level evidence for Switzerland
sources.publisher: Elizabeth Steiner and Yannic Stucki; Journal of International Money and Finance
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss manufacturing firm panel 2012–2017; Jan 2015 appreciation event
sources.revision: Published 2025; study sample 2012–2017
sources.units: Firm markups, exchange rates, sales invoicing
sources.scopeAndLimits: Reports heterogeneous markup adjustments after appreciation; large profitable exporters lower markups more, while average firm response is not significant. Event-study evidence does not establish present sector response or net GDP effect.

sources.title: Sectoral effects of exchange rate shocks: goods exports and the appreciation of the Swiss Franc in 2015
sources.publisher: Andreas Brunhart and Martin Geiger, Swiss Journal of Economics and Statistics
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss customs exports by sector; 2014–2016 around Jan 2015 appreciation
sources.revision: Open-access paper published 9 Jul 2025; historical counterfactual/event-study
sources.units: Nominal exports in CHF/EUR; real quantities; sectoral prices
sources.evidenceRole: Scholarly sector-level study using granular customs data
sources.scopeAndLimits: Finds heterogeneous sector adjustment; chemicals/pharma aggregate resilience and engineering/instruments exposure differ. Counterfactual relies on continuation of exchange-rate floor assumption; 2015 shock is not a direct estimate for 2026–30.

sources.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Switzerland 2024—EU integration and resilience
sources.publisher: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD)
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss–EU framework and global value chains; report uses earlier observation vintages
sources.revision: Survey published 2024; legal status predates Bilaterals III signature
sources.units: Trade costs, supply-chain links; qualitative policy analysis
sources.scopeAndLimits: Provides counterarguments: openness exposes shocks but supports diversification/productivity; EU access matters, while inward FDI and trade restrictions can have costs. It is not ex post evaluation of 2026 package.

sources.title: Notice to Stakeholders: Status of the EU-Switzerland Mutual Recognition Agreement for medical devices
sources.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Health and Food Safety
sources.observedPeriod: Medical-device MRA status from 26 May 2021
sources.revision: Official legal notice; 2021 status, package updates must be checked against later operative acts
sources.units: Regulatory access status, not numeric
sources.scopeAndLimits: Documents a concrete example of bilateral-market access discontinuity under the earlier framework, but is sector-specific and historical; the 2026 signed package must be evaluated for actual entry into force before assuming a remedy.

sources.title: GDP forecast: Swiss economy to grow moderately
sources.publisher: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), Expert Group on Business Cycles
sources.observedPeriod: Official conditional outlook 2026–2027
sources.revision: September 2026 forecast vintage; not observed outcomes
sources.units: Annual average CPI inflation and GDP growth, %
sources.scopeAndLimits: SECO conditional forecast reports average CPI inflation 0.6% in 2026 and 0.6% in 2027; this is distinct from SNB Sep 2026 forecast (0.7%, 0.8%) and realized monthly CPI. Forecast disagreement is evidence of vintage/model uncertainty, not contradiction in observed inflation.

sources.title: Consumer prices remained stable in September
sources.publisher: Swiss Federal Statistical Office (FSO), release distributed by SECO
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss CPI, September 2026
sources.revision: September 2026 release; later CPI revisions may occur
sources.units: CPI index points (Dec 2025=100); monthly and year-on-year percent change
sources.scopeAndLimits: September CPI headline and narrative price components (heating oil, petrol and diesel rose; international package holidays, car rental/car sharing and hotel prices fell). This release narrative does not quantify an imported-goods-only CPI component; no FX contribution is identified.

sources.title: Gross domestic product, quarterly data: Q2 2026 release
sources.observedPeriod: Swiss GDP, 2026-Q2; season/sport-event adjusted release
sources.revision: Quarterly national accounts vintage published 3 Sep 2026, incorporating BFS annual data revisions from 25 Aug 2026
sources.units: Quarter-on-quarter percent change; GDP levels and contributions in linked tables
sources.scopeAndLimits: Sport-event-adjusted growth was exceptionally strong and pharma/chemicals were a large contributor. Quarterly national accounts are revised; sectoral value added is volatile.

sources.title: FX risk premiums and the Swiss franc: a time-varying factor model
sources.observedPeriod: Daily EUR/CHF and USD/CHF sample 2006–2018
sources.revision: Working paper 2020-21; exact publication day not disclosed in reused preflight source metadata
sources.units: Exchange-rate returns; variance decomposition
sources.scopeAndLimits: Preflight literature notes risk factor contribution to CHF dynamics, especially under stress; historical decomposition is not a structural causal trade elasticity.

sources.title: Foreign exchange rates – monthly average, September 2026 (SNB data cube devkum)
sources.observedPeriod: Monthly-average CHF per EUR and CHF per USD, September 2026; data cube released 1 Oct 2026
sources.revision: CSV response identifies cube devkum and PublishingDate 2026-10-01 14:30; retrieved and parsed directly on 2026-10-14. Monthly mean, not a month-end spot observation.
sources.units: CHF per 1 EUR / CHF per 1 USD; monthly averages
sources.scopeAndLimits: Source URL selects EUR series; USD value retrieved with same cube and D1(USD1). Monthly average exchange rates do not measure firm-specific invoice exposure, realized hedging or effective exchange rate.

sources.title: Swiss balance of payments: merchanting sales of goods by type, quarterly (SNB data cube bopmercatq)
sources.observedPeriod: Gross merchanting sales of goods by type, 2026-Q2; cube last updated with Q2 2026 balance-of-payments release
sources.revision: Direct CSV API export on 2026-10-14; API PublishingDate 2026-09-22 09:00. Reported unit in CHF millions; category GT selected. Quarterly balance-of-payments data subject to revisions.
sources.units: CHF million, current-price gross sales; not value added or balance
sources.scopeAndLimits: GT is the total sales category per cube dimensions; value is gross sales of goods in merchanting, not merchanting margin, current-account balance, GDP contribution or trade-credit exposure. Interpret gross turnover separately from net earnings.

sources.title: Strengthening economic resilience within global value chains in Switzerland
sources.observedPeriod: Foreign-input reliance and product-level import concentration: principally 2018 input-output and 2002–2021 product-trade data; report published 2024
sources.revision: OECD 2024 Switzerland survey chapter; underlying data vintages/definitions cited at figure/table level. Product-level dependency filter applied to 2019 CEPII BACI data and persistence checked through 2021.
sources.units: Percent of foreign intermediate inputs by supplier region; import Herfindahl-Hirschman Index; product-country combinations
sources.evidenceRole: OECD analysis based on official input-output and CEPII product-level trade data
sources.scopeAndLimits: Foreign-input shares are 2018, not current. Report finds EU accounts for 54% of imported intermediate inputs on average, Asia 17%, North America 10%, rest of Europe 8%, other 11%; average import concentration fell 7% between 2002 and 2021. Roughly 60 country-product combinations remained at risk two years after 2019. These are structural exposure indicators, not observed 2026 relocation or causal friendshoring gains.

sources.title: Chemical and pharmaceutical industries remain the backbone
sources.publisher: scienceindustries (Swiss business association; statistics sourced to Swiss customs / Swiss-Impex)
sources.observedPeriod: Chemical, pharmaceutical and life-science merchandise exports, calendar year 2025
sources.revision: Association release dated 29 Jan 2026 reports Swiss-Impex/Federal Customs Administration data; classification combines chemical, pharmaceutical and life-science products.
sources.units: Nominal customs goods exports, CHF billion; share of total merchandise exports
sources.evidenceRole: Industry association release using Swiss-Impex customs totals; not national accounts
sources.scopeAndLimits: Reports CHF 152.1bn exports in 2025, +2.2% y/y and over 52% of total Swiss merchandise exports. Group definition can differ from FOCBS tariff group and export values are neither real volume nor Swiss value added; association has an industry-promotion role. Cross-check against official FOCBS 2024 data: CHF 149.1bn and 52.7% of exports.

sources.title: Swiss foreign trade in 2024
sources.publisher: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG)
sources.observedPeriod: Detailed customs merchandise exports by product group, calendar year 2024
sources.revision: Annual report table/text: chemical and pharmaceutical product exports CHF 149.1bn, 52.7% of total merchandise exports in 2024; caution noted on tariff-structure simplifications for comparisons.
sources.units: Nominal customs merchandise exports, CHF billion and percent share
sources.scopeAndLimits: Nominal goods exports do not equal domestic value added, real quantities or company cash receipts; tariff classification changes constrain comparisons across years.

sources.title: Swiss foreign trade, Q1 2026; seasonally adjusted exports, Annex Ia
sources.publisher: Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS/BAZG)
sources.observedPeriod: 2026-Q1 versus 2025-Q4, seasonally adjusted nominal quarter-on-quarter
sources.revision: Official FOCBS release PDF dated 21 Apr 2026; quarterly customs series subject to revision. Raw PDF archived at raw/focbs_q1_2026_annex.pdf (HTTP 200 application/pdf).
sources.units: CHF million seasonally adjusted nominal exports; percent q/q change
sources.evidenceRole: Primary FOCBS quarterly merchandise-trade annex, Annex Ia.
sources.scopeAndLimits: Chemical and pharmaceutical exports are customs flows, not output/value added or identified CHF effects. Annex Ia headings explicitly say seasonally adjusted and change vs prior quarter; no year-on-year rate is reported for this row.

sources.title: OECD Economic Surveys: Switzerland 2026
sources.observedPeriod: Current Swiss macroeconomic and structural assessment; report publication dated 15 Sep 2026; underlying data vintages vary by chapter
sources.revision: OECD 2026 Switzerland Survey; current overview says recent shocks handled comparatively well, while trade/geopolitical uncertainty leaves small open economy vulnerable; no estimated causal friendshoring coefficient cited in reviewed summary.
sources.units: Qualitative macroeconomic assessment; units vary by chapter
sources.scopeAndLimits: Useful current counterweight on resilience and external vulnerability; does not quantify supply-chain relocation or net friendshoring gains. Reviewed abstract/summary only; detailed sector evidence remains from older OECD chapter and must be cited as such.

sources.title: Import Price Index, detailed results, August 2026 (FSO table 05.04.04.02)
sources.observedPeriod: Monthly import price indices through 2026-08; Dec 2025=100 index basis; monthly and year-on-year comparisons computed from the source series
sources.revision: Direct FSO DAM XLSX downloaded 2026-10-14; workbook covers 2003-05 through 2026-08 and uses the 2025 index revision. Raw XLSX archived at raw/fso_import_detail_aug2026.xlsx (HTTP 200, 901053 bytes).
sources.units: Import-price index points (December 2025=100); computed percent change
sources.evidenceRole: Primary FSO monthly series, detailed import-price categories.
sources.scopeAndLimits: Index levels and index changes are not CPI contributions or causal exchange-rate pass-through. August 2026 is the latest observation publicly released by cutoff; September series release was scheduled after 2026-10-14.

sources.title: Balance of payments, current-account balance, quarterly (SNB cube bopoverq)
sources.observedPeriod: 2026-Q2 net current-account balance; includes goods, services and income balances, not a merchanting-only series
sources.revision: SNB API CSV PublishingDate 2026-09-22 09:00; quarterly balance-of-payments estimates are subject to revisions. Raw CSV archived at raw/snb_bopoverq_q2.csv (HTTP 200).
sources.units: CHF million, net current-account balance
sources.evidenceRole: Primary SNB balance-of-payments cube; direct net balance series.
sources.scopeAndLimits: S0 is the total current-account net balance. Cube dimensions do not isolate merchanting. The Q2 release states merchanting balance increased significantly year on year but gives no numeric merchanting-only balance in its narrative; total current account is not a proxy for merchanting.

sources.title: Publication dates for the Producer and Import Price Index in 2026
sources.observedPeriod: 2026 release calendar; September 2026 index release date
sources.revision: Official FSO schedule PDF retrieved 2026-10-14; raw copy at raw/fso_ipi_release_schedule_2026.pdf (HTTP 200 application/pdf).
sources.units: Scheduled publication date
sources.scopeAndLimits: Page 2 lists September import-price release on 15 October 2026, after this research cutoff of 14 October 2026; a schedule is not an observed index value.
